title: Maui's Family Across Island Accounts
subtitle: Names and kinship vary across the collected versions

learningObjectives.text: What pattern repeats across the Maui accounts?
How do the island versions differ?

family.work: Legends of Ma-Ui, a Demi God of Polynesia and of his Mother Hina
family.author: W. D. Westervelt
family.locator: Chapter I · MAUI'S HOME; Chapter I · MAUI'S HOME, normalized characters 2031-2317
family.excerpt: In the Hawaiian chant, Akalana was the name of his father. In other groups this was the name by which his mother was known. Kanaloa, the god, is sometimes known as the father of Maui. In Hawaii Hina was his mother. Elsewhere Ina, or Hina, was the grandmother, from whom he secured fire.
family.note: Verbatim prose from Westervelt's early twentieth-century English compilation. Retain the named island/version; this is not a direct transcription of one oral performance.

narrativeBlocks.title: A hero with many homes
narrativeBlocks.body: Maui is the great Polynesian culture-hero — and he belongs to no single island: Hawaii, New Zealand, Samoa, Tonga, and more each claim their own Maui, and the tales braid versions together.

narrativeBlocks.title: The miraculous birth
narrativeBlocks.body: Nearly everywhere the pattern repeats: Maui is the unwanted fifth son — thrown into the sea in his mother's topknot or afterbirth — rescued by the gods, raised away, returning as the youngest and cleverest.

narrativeBlocks.title: The trickster's job
narrativeBlocks.body: He is not a war-hero: Maui's tools are nerve and cunning — he fishes islands from the sea, slows the sun, steals fire, tries to win immortality. The world's conveniences are his pranks.

narrativeBlocks.title: The family that doubts him
narrativeBlocks.body: His four brothers are the story's skeptics — they mock his claims, then watch him do the impossible anyway. Doubt-then-wonder is the pattern every episode repeats.

narrativeBlocks.title: One hero, many cultures
narrativeBlocks.body: Westervelt's collection gathers the island accounts side by side — so we can see the same trickster wearing different local details across the whole Pacific.

quiz.prompt: What is consistent across the island accounts of Maui?

choices.text: He is always the eldest son
He is a war-god of each island
The pattern: unwanted youngest son, rescued by gods, returns to do impossible feats with cunning
He is born at sea and raised by fish

quiz.explanation: The structure repeats across the Pacific; only the local details change.

quiz.explanation: The doubters-turned-witnesses are the tales' rhythm.
